claim.statement: GitLab's current documentation says runner-executed flows use a one-time composite identity combining the initiating human with a Developer-role service account, applying the more restrictive role and project-access intersection.

source.title: Composite identity
source.locator: How composite identity works and Composite identity workflow

values: intersection of human and service-account project access

lifecycle.reason: Automatic inclusion after the 18.9 setting removal.

limitations: This is GitLab's described authorization design, not an observed token or permission trace.
OAuth ai_workflows and mcp scopes and CI job-token permissions are distinct; the statement does not collapse them.
unknowns: The human user, service account, effective role, project intersection and token contents for any execution are unknown.
The exact token implementation and audit-log representation per offering were not inspected.

relationships.note: Current automatic inclusion follows the 18.8 configurable state and 18.9 setting removal.
